Case_08015/figure3.jpg.source_caption: H and E stain of specimen, higher (40x) magnification.

description.short_caption: H&E stain showing fungal organisms with surrounding inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This is a histopathology image stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at high magnification (40x). The image shows fungal organisms, characterized by round to oval structures with clear halos, suggestive of a capsule. These structures are surrounded by an inflammatory infiltrate, including numerous darkly stained nuclei of inflammatory cells. The background tissue appears disrupted, with areas of necrosis and pink-staining extracellular matrix.
visible_findings: round to oval fungal organisms with clear halos
inflammatory cell infiltrate with dark nuclei

Case_08015/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin (H and E) stain of spleen specimen, low magnification.

description.short_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of spleen specimen at low magnification.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a spleen specimen stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at low magnification. The tissue displays a mix of red and purple staining, with areas of red likely representing vascular or hemorrhagic regions and purple areas corresponding to cellular components. The architecture suggests a disrupted or inflamed spleen, with possible infiltration or necrosis visible in some regions. The image is de-identified and labeled for educational purposes.
visible_findings: red and purple staining typical of H&E
areas of potential necrosis or infiltration

description.short_caption: Coronal CT scan of the abdomen showing intra-abdominal pathology.
description.detailed_description: This is a coronal CT scan of the abdomen. The image shows soft tissue structures, bowel loops, and abdominal organs. There appears to be abnormal soft tissue density in the mid-abdomen, possibly suggestive of an infectious or inflammatory process. The bowel loops are visible, and there may be evidence of mesenteric involvement or lymphadenopathy. No contrast enhancement is evident, suggesting this is a non-contrast study.
visible_findings: soft tissue density in the mid-abdomen

Case_08015/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Mucicarmine stain of spleen specimen, 40x magnification.

description.short_caption: Mucicarmine stain of spleen specimen showing encapsulated yeast forms, 40x magnification.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a mucicarmine-stained section of a spleen specimen at 40x magnification. Numerous round to oval yeast forms with prominent capsules are visible, stained bright pink to red, against a lighter background. The mucicarmine stain highlights the polysaccharide capsule of the organisms, which is a key diagnostic feature. The background tissue appears faintly stained, allowing the yeast forms to stand out clearly.
